features.claim: Tylosaurus had a long, toothless snout knob sticking out from its snout.
features.quote: The most recognizable characteristic of Tylosaurus is the elongated edentulous rostrum that protrudes from its snout, for which the genus is named.

features.claim: The head of Tylosaurus was strongly conical and its snout was longer than most mosasaurs.
features.quote: The head was strongly conical and the snout proportionally longer than most mosasaurs, with the exception of Ectenosaurus.

features.claim: Tylosaurus had small diamond-shaped scales arranged in oblique rows.
features.quote: These scales were small and diamond-shaped and were arranged in oblique rows, comparable to that found in modern rattlesnakes and other related reptiles.

features.claim: Tylosaurus was dark colored in life, like a leatherback sea turtle.
features.quote: Microscopic analysis of scales in a T. nepaeolicus specimen by Lindgren et al. (2014) detected high traces of the pigment eumelanin indicative of a dark coloration similar to the leatherback sea turtle in life.

features.claim: Tylosaurus had teeth with finely serrated cutting edges in T. rex and sometimes T. proriger.
features.quote: Carinae (cutting edges) are finely serrated with small denticles in T. rex and sometimes T. proriger, which appear similar to those in Prognathodon and Mosasaurus though not as developed as in theropod dinosaurs or living monitors, and smooth in T. nepaeolicus and T. kansasensis.

features.claim: Tylosaurus had 2 teeth in each premaxilla, 12 to 13 in each maxilla, 13 in each dentary, and 10 to 11 in each pterygoid.
features.quote: On each side of the skull, Tylosaurus had 2 premaxillary teeth, 12 to 13 maxillary teeth, 13 dentary teeth, and 10 to 11 pterygoid teeth.

features.claim: The largest well-known Tylosaurus specimen was estimated at around 13.2 meters long.
features.quote: More recent estimates have suggested a more precise size of around 13.2 meters (43 ft), with the species as a whole ranging between 7.7–13.2 meters (25–43 ft).

features.claim: Tylosaurus was a large, predatory marine lizard.
features.quote: It was a  large, predatory marine lizard closely related to modern monitor lizards and to snakes.

not_this.claim: Older pictures showed Tylosaurus with a long neck, but that is wrong.
not_this.quote: This reconstruction was subsequently adopted in various works published during the late 19th century, although some authors also portrayed the animal with a long neck.

not_this.claim: Older pictures showed Tylosaurus with only front flippers and no back ones, but that is wrong.
not_this.quote: Still according to Cope, the animal would have had only the flippers located at the front of the body, those at the back being absent.

not_this.claim: Older pictures showed Tylosaurus as a giant flippered sea snake, but that is wrong.
not_this.quote: While in the past derived mosasaurs were depicted as akin to giant flippered sea snakes, it is now understood that they were more similar in build to other large marine vertebrates such as ichthyosaurs, marine crocodylomorphs, and archaeocete whales through convergent evolution.

not_this.claim: Older pictures showed Tylosaurus moving by undulating its whole body like a snake, but that is wrong.
not_this.quote: Scientists previously interpreted Tylosaurus as an anguilliform swimmer that moved by undulating its entire body like a snake due to its close relationship with the animal.

debated.claim: It is unknown how dark and light pigments were arranged on the body of Tylosaurus.
debated.quote: This may have been complemented with countershading, present in many aquatic animals, though the distribution of dark and light pigments in the species remains unknown.
